title: Assistant Accountant
description:
Assistant Accountant

Stokenchurch Competitive salary, study support & good benefits Hybrid working

Are you a commercially minded, part-qualified accountant looking for a role where your analysis genuinely shapes business decisions?

We are seeking a proactive Assistant Accountant to join an established and growing commercial finance team in Stokenchurch. This is an excellent opportunity for an ambitious AAT, CIMA or ACCA studier to take ownership of meaningful commercial reporting, work closely with operational and client-facing colleagues, and develop within a collaborative, fast-paced environment.

You will sit at the centre of financial performance, helping to protect profitability, improve commercial visibility and turn financial data into clear, practical insight for stakeholders across the business.

The opportunity

Reporting to the Commercial Accounting Manager, you will support the delivery of accurate management information and robust financial control across revenue, cost of sales, gross profit and client or business-unit performance.

This is not a purely transactional accounting position. You will be encouraged to question, investigate, identify opportunities and communicate the story behind the numbers to non-financial stakeholders.

Key responsibilities
- Prepare and review monthly management accounts, including revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, accruals, prepayments and balance-sheet reconciliations.
- Analyse client, project, cost-centre and business-unit performance, identifying key variances, commercial risks and opportunities.
- Partner with internal teams and clients to prepare budgets, ensuring assumptions are robust and profitability is protected through appropriate inflationary and rate-card adjustments.
- Support forecasting and financial-planning activity with accurate data and commercially focused analysis.
- Produce clear, concise financial commentary for senior stakeholders to support informed decision-making.
- Maintain strong financial controls and ensure compliance with internal policies, accounting standards and audit requirements.
- Support month-end, year-end, statutory reporting and external audit processes.
- Identify and deliver improvements to reporting, processes, controls and the quality of commercial insight.
- Undertake ad-hoc analysis and finance projects in line with changing business priorities.

About you

You will be a confident and curious finance professional who enjoys understanding how a business operates-not simply reporting the results.

You will ideally bring:
- Part-qualified AAT, CIMA or ACCA status, with a commitment to completing your qualification.
- Previous experience within a commercial accounting, management accounting or finance business-partnering environment.
- Strong Excel capability and confidence handling, analysing and interpreting financial data.
- A sound understanding of revenue, costs, margins, budgets, forecasts and financial performance.
- The ability to communicate complex financial information clearly to colleagues outside finance.
- A proactive, improvement-focused mindset, with the confidence to challenge constructively and ask the right questions.
- An interest in keeping up to date with financial reporting requirements, regulatory developments and commercial finance best practice.
- Experience of PeopleSoft and/or Planning Analytics would be advantageous, but is not essential.

Why apply?

This role offers broad commercial exposure and the opportunity to make a visible contribution to the performance of the business. You will work closely with stakeholders across finance, operations and client teams, gaining the experience needed to progress your commercial finance career.

Alongside a competitive salary of 30-35k (depending on experience), you will receive a benefits package designed to support your professional development, financial wellbeing and work-life balance, including:
- A study support package for employees working towards their AAT, CIMA or ACCA qualification.
- Pension scheme.
- Life assurance cover.
- Income protection.
- 26 days' annual leave, plus bank holidays.
- Hybrid working - 3 days in the office.

If you are a capable part-qualified accountant seeking a role with genuine stakeholder engagement, ownership and development potential, we would welcome your application.

title: Remote Conveyancing Paralegal
company: LEGAL TALENT PARTNERS LIMITED - Agency - Permanent
description:
Remote Conveyancing Paralegal

£30,000-40,000

Quality. Technology. Flexibility. A Better Way to Do Conveyancing.

We're partnering with a fast-growing, forward-thinking residential conveyancing firm that is using technology, smarter processes and a collaborative team structure to change the way property law is delivered.

The firm is built around a simple idea: conveyancing should be simpler, clearer and faster - for clients and the people delivering it.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for greater autonomy, better technology, a sustainable workload and the flexibility of a fully remote role, this could be an excellent next move.

Why This Role Stands Out

This is not a traditional conveyancing environment where paralegals are left to manage overwhelming caseloads with little support.

You'll work within small, collaborative teams, with regular check-ins, structured 1-to-1s, feedback and personalised training.

The firm takes a quality over quantity approach to workload, maintaining sustainable caseloads and giving teams capacity to deal with peaks without compromising client service.

You'll benefit from:
- Sustainable caseloads and a strong focus on work-life balance
- Small, collaborative teams
- Regular support, feedback and development
- Bespoke technology designed around legal teams
- A culture where asking for help is encouraged
- The opportunity to influence how technology and processes develop
- Fully remote working with genuine flexibility

The result? A more manageable workload, better support and the freedom to focus on delivering excellent conveyancing rather than simply processing as many files as possible.

The Role

As a Conveyancing Paralegal, you'll be an integral part of a residential conveyancing team, working alongside lawyers and other paralegals to deliver an excellent client service.

You'll work across freehold and leasehold sales, purchases and remortgages, taking ownership of your matters while working collaboratively with the wider team.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Progressing residential sales, purchases and remortgages
- Handling freehold sales with minimal supervision
- Managing most leasehold sale enquiries with minimal supervision
- Managing most freehold purchase enquiries with minimal supervision
- Liaising with clients, solicitors, estate agents and other third parties
- Proactively identifying issues and keeping transactions moving
- Reviewing and responding to enquiries
- Maintaining clear, jargon-free communication
- Using the firm's technology to manage your caseload efficiently
- Identifying and resolving potential issues before they become blockers
- Providing feedback to improve systems and processes

The firm's technology has been developed specifically around its conveyancing process, and legal professionals are encouraged to provide feedback on the tools they use every day.

About you

You'll ideally have:
- Strong experience in residential conveyancing
- Experience handling freehold sales with limited supervision
- Experience dealing with leasehold sale enquiries
- Experience dealing with freehold purchase enquiries
- Confidence communicating with clients and third parties
- A proactive approach to progressing transactions
- Strong organisation and attention to detail
- Excellent communication and problem-solving skills
- Confidence working independently in a remote environment
- An interest in using technology to improve legal work

You don't need to be qualified. This role is suited to an experienced paralegal with strong technical conveyancing skills who is ready to take greater ownership of their work.

Although fully remote, you won't be left alone with a laptop and a pile of files. Regular team check-ins, 1-to-1s and ongoing feedback are built into the firm's approach.

The Culture:

This is a firm deliberately doing things differently.

Rather than chasing maximum utilisation, it takes a sustainable approach to workload, helping teams maintain consistent service levels while giving people room to deal with the unexpected.

Its technology helps allocate work, streamline processes and keep teams informed, while its remote-working model is built around communication, supervision, feedback and development.

There's also a strong culture of transparency and continuous improvement. People are encouraged to share ideas, challenge processes and help shape the future of the business.

The Package
- £30,000-£40,000 depending on experience
- Fully remote - work from anywhere in the UK
- Flexible working hours
- 25 days' holiday + 3 days at Christmas + Bank Holidays
- Full home-working setup and equipment provided
- Comprehensive private healthcare
- Free access to Spill mental health and wellbeing support
- Company pension scheme
- Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption leave
- Growth Shares, giving employees an opportunity to share in the long-term success of the business
- Fully paid-for annual company weekend
- Structured development and genuine progression opportunities

The firm's flexible approach is a key part of its culture, with many employees working flexible hours or part-time. The focus is on creating working patterns that work for both the individual and the wider team.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for a genuinely modern, supportive and flexible place to build your career, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Accounts and Purchasing Administrator
description:
Accounts and Purchasing Administrator

Milton Keynes

Salary: circa £30,000 per annum

Hours 8.30 -5pm

Free Parking

We are recruiting on behalf of a well-established and successful international organisation for an Accounts, Purchasing Administrator to join their busy team in Milton Keynes.

This varied role will support the Accounts, Purchasing and Administration functions, ensuring the smooth running of financial processes while providing administrative support across multiple departments. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys a hands-on role and thrives in a fast-paced environment where accuracy and attention to detail are essential.

The Role

Reporting to the Accounts, Purchasing and Administration Supervisor, you will be responsible for supporting accounts payable, purchasing activities and general office administration.

Key Responsibilities

Accounts Payable & Finance
- Processing and coding supplier invoices
- Posting vouchers and payment transactions within the ERP system
- Managing Accounts Payable ledgers and reconciliations
- Processing employee expenses through Concur and manual systems
- Creating Accounts Payable payment runs
- Performing vendor statement reconciliations
- Investigating and reconciling freight invoices
- Supporting General Ledger reconciliations
- Producing cash requirement reports
- Maintaining supplier records and vendor spreadsheets
- Recording Postponed VAT Accounting transactions

Purchasing
- Raising and issuing purchase orders
- Monitoring goods receipt and supplier invoices
- Supporting supplier management and maintaining competitive pricing
- Conducting supplier research and price comparisons
- Carrying out regular pricing reviews
- Ensuring purchasing procedures are maintained and updated

Administration
- Reviewing credit applications
- Managing petty cash and month-end reporting
- Providing reception cover, including answering calls and welcoming visitors
- Maintaining filing systems and company records
- Coordinating travel, accommodation and visitor arrangements
- Supporting trade show administration and expenditure tracking
- Monitoring and distributing marketing materials
- Providing general administrative support across departments
- Supporting Accounts Receivable and wider administration teams when required

About You

To be successful in this role, you will have:
- Previous Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable and Purchasing experience ideally
- Strong administration and organisational skills
- Excellent attention to detail and accuracy
- Strong numerical and analytical abilities
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel
- Experience working with ERP or finance systems

Personal Attributes
- Self-motivated with a proactive approach
- Strong problem-solving skills and ability to use initiative
- Comfortable working independently and as part of a small team
- Professional, confident and personable manner
- Able to manage multiple priorities and work under pressure
- Highly organised with strong planning skills
- Flexible approach to supporting business needs
- Full driving licence preferred

If you're looking for a varied position that combines accounts, purchasing and administration, and you enjoy working in a collaborative environment where no two days are the same, we'd love to hear from you.

description:
Accounts & Purchasing Administrator

This role offers the opportunity to work within a small growing team with a global manufacturer. The ability to contribute to a professional, detail-focused team where accuracy, reliability and teamwork are essential to smooth day-to-day operations.

A background in accounts payable, purchase ledger and purchasing administration experience who enjoys working with detail, deadlines and supplier information.

- Excellent attention to detail, accurate data entry skills and a procedure-driven approach.
- Good numeracy and the ability to investigate and resolve discrepancies.
- Strong organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise work, meet deadlines and manage varied tasks.

BENEFITS: Excellent additional bens

Main Purpose of the role:

A fantastic opportunity has arisen for a Paralegal to join a highly regarded law firm and join its Criminal or Regulatory Dispute Resolution team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to build theirlegal career within a specialist practice, working on a varied range of matters for both private individuals and business clients. The successful candidate will ideally have some experience in Criminal Law, Regulatory Law or Dispute Resolution, together with strong research, drafting and organisational skills.

- Providing comprehensive Paralegal support to the legal team.
- Assisting Solicitors with a varied caseload of Criminal and Regulatory Dispute Resolution matters.
- Assisting with motoring offences, including speeding, drink/drug driving, careless and dangerous driving and other road traffic matters.

- Providing a consistently high standard of client care and professional service.

- Alternatively, experience in Regulatory Dispute Resolution or wider criminal matters.

- Good knowledge of legal procedures and case management.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
